2609.34886.title: Fewer Assumptions by Design: A Reusable Skill for LLM-Assisted Verus Verification
2609.34886.paper_summary: LLM-assisted Verus verification is a less tedious method to verify Rust implementations, but paired with self-referential structures, e.g., Doubly Linked Lists (DLLs)ânotoriously difficult to formalise for verificationâit becomes a substantially more demanding verification task.    Moreover, a specification weakness can arise when verification relies on unproven or invalidated assumptions, such as axiomatic lemmas and assume statements. We investigate whether LLM agents can synthesize strong DLL specifications while minimizing these trusted base. The analysis follows three different approaches: manual verification, property-specific verification, and a defined skill for the specific case of DLLs and certain properties of this type of data structure. The skill encodes domain knowledge and a task-decomposition strategy. We show that an LLM agent equipped with a carefully designed verification skill can generate strong, low-trust specifications for DLLs in Verus.
2609.34886.paper_summary_zh: LLM輔助的Verus驗證是一種較不繁瑣的方法來驗證Rust實現，但當與自參考結構（例如，雙向鏈表（DLL））結合時——這些結構在驗證上 notoriously 難以形式化——它變成了一個實質上更具挑戰性的驗證任務。<lb/>此外，當驗證依賴於未經證明或無效的假設時，例如公理引理和假設語句，可能會出現規範弱點。我們研究LLM代理是否能在最小化這些可信基礎的同時合成強大的DLL規範。<lb/>分析遵循三種不同的方法：手動驗證、特定性質的驗證，以及針對DLL及此類數據結構某些性質的特定案例所定義的技能。<lb/>該技能編碼了領域知識和任務分解策略。我們展示了一個配備精心設計的驗證技能的LLM代理能夠為Verus中的DLL生成強大且低信任的規範。
